new_statements.quote: There are six live tones: two level (55, 33), two rising (35, 13), one falling (31) and the slight tone (atonality) 'ø'. The slight tone 'ø' appears only in some prefixes. The dead tones have pitch shapes 55, 33, 31. [...] Tonal change is common in context, and many cases show progressive assimilation [...] (p. 141). [...] There are two main types of derivation: prefix + head, head + suffix. All prefixes are pronounced with tone, but a few of them are pronounced with the slight tone. (p. 144)
new_statements.citation: Li Jinfang. 1996. Bugan -- a new Mon-Khmer language of Yunnan Province, China. Mon-Khmer Studies 26: 135-159.
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened: (lines 340-520 read) and page images and MKS 26 p. 141); (extracted text); the Edmondson & Li 1996 and Edmondson & Gregerson 1996 scanned files and Hsiu 2016 texts under buga1251/ and buga1247/; the earlier Google Books snippet JSONs under buga1247/googlebooks_snippets/. QUOTE: p. 141 sec. 1.3 'Tones' reads on the page image exactly 'There are six live tones: two level (55, 33), two rising (35, 13), one falling (31) and the slight tone (atonality) 'ø'. The slight tone 'ø' appears only in some prefixes. The dead tones have pitch shapes 55, 33, 31.' followed by 'Tones are instable in Bugan.. Tonal change is common in context, and many cases show progressive assimilation..' -- verbatim…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Bugan is described purely as a lexical-tone language (five contrastive tones on full syllables plus checked-syllable tones); the only prominence asymmetry mentioned is that some prefixal (minor) syllables are toneless ('slight tone/atonality', i.e. a neutral tone), implying weak presyllable + full tonal root, but the author never uses the terms stress or accent and gives no rule for word stress.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. Tones are 'instable' (lexical doublets with two tones) and undergo extensive contextual sandhi; toneless 'slight tone' restricted to a subset of prefixes (e.g. pə0-, tə0-), other prefixes carry full tones (pə55-, te55-, mu33-..).
new_statements.domain_note: Citation forms of words (mostly monosyllables; disyllables = prefix + root or compounds). Same wording is repeated second-hand in Edmondson & Li 1996 p. 987 and Edmondson & Gregerson 1996 p. 119 ('one 0 (atonal) prosody appearing on some prefixes'); Li & Luo 2015 p. 1039 (snippet): 'Prefixes can carry lexical tones; a few take the neutral tone.'
new_statements.identity_note: buga1251 is a Glottolog bookkeeping entry for the retired ISO code [bgh] "Bogan". ISO 639-3 Change Request 2006-050 (saved:) merged [bgh] into [bbh] Bugan: "bgh refers to the same language as bbh.. these two ISO codes were created as information on this language came from two different sources under two slightly different names" (autonym [pə55 ka̤n33]). Every descriptive source is therefore a source for buga1247 Bugan; the quoted description (Li 1996) is of the Nala/Manlong-area variety studied by Li Jinfang. Cataloguing buga1251 separately would double-count Bugan; any catalog entry belongs under buga1247.
